lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Put Lumen before Westfield in Experience.
items.because: The section should be in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Consider placing Experience before Education.
items.because: Experience and project results are the strongest evidence for general front-end roles.

items.says: Check that the code link leads to a current, accessible profile or portfolio with relevant work.
items.because: The text alone does not tell readers what the link contains.

items.says: Clarify the scope of “owned.”
items.because: Readers need to understand what you were responsible for.

items.says: Verify that the monthly broken-page counts were measured consistently.
Make sure the relationship between preview mode and the reduction in broken pages is supportable.
Clarify what “failed audits” means.
Confirm whether the checklist was adopted across all university pages as stated.
Define and verify how “search time” was measured.
items.because: It could mean user task time or system response time, which are different claims.

items.says: Specify the performance measure behind the 35% improvement.
items.because: “Page performance” is too broad to interpret on its own.

items.says: Specify which pages or experience the improvement covers.
Identify the accessibility audit’s scope or standard if available.
items.because: The bullet should not imply broader compliance than the audit established.

items.says: Make clear that the test and regression numbers refer to your work.
Recheck the LCP improvement and its attribution to lazy-loading the hero image.
items.because: Lazy-loading a hero image visible immediately can delay loading and worsen LCP.

items.says: Clarify the scope of “median load time.”
Clarify the A/B-test result and avoid overstating its attribution.
items.because: The booking increase should be attributed only as strongly as the experiment supports.

items.says: Storing input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML does not prevent XSS.
Explain how the estimate of about 900 riders a week was obtained.
Clarify what “live” means for the data source or update behavior.
Verify that the 0.8s and 2.9s figures came from a fair, consistent measurement.
Clarify what the timing measures and the test conditions.
Check that the repository and agency developer-page link are public and current.
The heading lists Vue, but the project bullet lists React and TypeScript.
items.because: The project technologies and bullets should describe the same project.

items.says: The React and TypeScript stack conflicts with the heading’s Vue stack.
Distinguish your booking-flow contribution from the team’s work.
The travel-search result appears to repeat the Lumen accomplishment and may not belong to Library Room Booking.
items.because: Its current placement makes the project history difficult to trust.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
Review whether Angular belongs in the tools list.
items.because: Without an example, it may invite questions about your level of experience.

items.says: Be ready to support the broad methods listed with concrete examples.
items.because: The terms, especially accessibility and server-side rendering, are broad.
